flagshipSystems.title: Enterprise Hybrid RAG Platform
flagshipSystems.tagline: Dense Semantic + BM25 Lexical Retrieval with Reciprocal Rank Fusion & RAGAS
flagshipSystems.problem: Pure dense vector retrieval consistently misses exact SKU identifiers, error codes, and technical domain jargon, while generating ungrounded answers without strict sentence-level citation provenance.
flagshipSystems.solution: Built a production-grade dual-retrieval architecture combining dense embeddings (HNSW in pgvector) and sparse BM25 indices, unified through Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and scored by a Cross-Encoder Reranker before LLM generation.

pipeline.name: Documents
pipeline.detail: Extracts text, structural hierarchy, and tables from multi-page PDFs, markdown, and docx files.
pipeline.tradeoff: Rule-based parsing is 10x faster than vision LLMs, but requires fallback OCR on scanned documents.

pipeline.name: Parsing & Chunking
pipeline.detail: Sliding-window chunking (400 tokens with 50 token overlap) aligned on paragraph and heading boundaries.
pipeline.tradeoff: Small chunks (200 tokens) increase retrieval precision but lose broad context; 400 tokens balances context density.

pipeline.name: Embeddings
pipeline.detail: Generates 1536-dimensional normalized dense vectors capturing deep semantic relationships.
pipeline.tradeoff: Large embedding models incur slightly higher API latency but reduce cross-domain cluster confusion.

pipeline.name: PostgreSQL + pgvector
pipeline.detail: Persists embeddings alongside relational document metadata with HNSW index for sub-10ms approximate nearest neighbor search.
pipeline.tradeoff: HNSW uses more RAM than IVFFlat but delivers significantly higher recall under concurrent querying.

pipeline.name: Dense + BM25 Hybrid
pipeline.detail: Queries both dense vector embeddings (for semantic intent) and sparse BM25 index (for exact acronyms, IDs, and tokens).
pipeline.tradeoff: Running dual search adds ~15ms retrieval overhead, but eliminates 85%+ of zero-result lexical queries.

pipeline.name: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
pipeline.detail: Merges disparate ranking distributions using RRF score = Σ [1 / (60 + rank_i)], eliminating fragile manual score thresholds.
pipeline.tradeoff: RRF is parameter-free and resilient across domains, though it ignores raw confidence magnitudes.

pipeline.name: Cross-Encoder Reranker
pipeline.detail: Applies joint self-attention across query-passage pairs on top 30 candidates to select top 5 highest-relevance contexts.
pipeline.tradeoff: Cross-encoders have O(N) inference cost, making them suited only for candidate reranking, not initial retrieval.

pipeline.name: LLM Reasoning
pipeline.detail: Synthesizes final answer constrained strictly to provided contexts with chain-of-thought verification.
pipeline.tradeoff: Strict prompt grounding prevents hallucination but increases token cost and reasoning latency.

pipeline.name: Citations & Attribution
pipeline.detail: Enforces JSON schema output requiring bracketed paragraph citations and source document IDs.
pipeline.tradeoff: Schema validation can occasionally trigger retries if the model generates loose formatting.

pipeline.name: Evaluation
pipeline.detail: Evaluates synthetic test queries measuring Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, Context Precision, and Context Recall.
pipeline.tradeoff: Automated LLM-as-judge evaluation costs compute, but provides objective CI/CD regression protection.

engineeringDecisions: Chose PostgreSQL + pgvector over standalone vector DBs to eliminate distributed synchronization between metadata and vectors.
Implemented Hybrid Search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion to solve the classic 'rare keyword' failure mode in dense-only retrieval.
Integrated Cross-Encoder reranking to boost Top-5 NDCG before passing context into the LLM context window.

flagshipSystems.title: Agentic AI Operations Platform
flagshipSystems.tagline: Multi-Agent LangGraph Supervisor with Model Context Protocol (MCP) & Checkpointed State
flagshipSystems.problem: Single monolithic prompts and linear chain architectures fail on complex multi-step workflows requiring branching logic, specialized tool calling, state recovery, and human governance.
flagshipSystems.solution: Architected a graph-based multi-agent system using LangGraph with a Supervisor Node coordinating specialized sub-agents (RAG, SQL, Web Research, API Tools) communicating via standardized MCP protocols.

pipeline.name: User Input
pipeline.detail: Accepts high-level user objective and conversational context.
pipeline.tradeoff: Requires input sanitization and schema validation before graph execution.

pipeline.name: LangGraph Supervisor
pipeline.detail: Maintains shared state, analyzes progress, and dynamically routes next action to the best-suited agent.
pipeline.tradeoff: Supervisor model latency is incurred at each routing step, but enables adaptive multi-step planning.

pipeline.name: Specialized Sub-Agents
pipeline.detail: Four autonomous agents with restricted prompt instructions, individual system prompts, and scoped tools.
pipeline.tradeoff: Domain isolation reduces agent confusion but requires clear handoff schemas between agents.

pipeline.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
pipeline.detail: Decouples tool implementations into standardized RPC services for database reads, API calls, and file actions.
pipeline.tradeoff: Protocol serialization overhead (~3ms) in exchange for language-agnostic modularity and reusability.

pipeline.name: Postgres Checkpointer
pipeline.detail: Persists state at every node transition, enabling time-travel debugging, session resumption, and human-in-the-loop pauses.
pipeline.tradeoff: Database writes on every graph step slightly increase turn latency, but guarantee 100% crash resilience.

pipeline.name: HITL Verification
pipeline.detail: Halts execution for human confirmation whenever agents attempt destructive actions (e.g. database updates, emails).
pipeline.tradeoff: Introduces asynchronous user delay for safety-critical operations.

pipeline.name: Synthesis & Response
pipeline.detail: Supervisor verifies that all sub-agent deliverables satisfy user criteria and returns a unified verified response.
pipeline.tradeoff: Final aggregation pass ensures cohesive voice across disparate worker outputs.

engineeringDecisions: Implemented cyclical graph architecture in LangGraph rather than linear DAGs to permit self-correction and retry loops.
Employed Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers to allow tools to be shared securely across multiple internal AI services.
Integrated PostgreSQL checkpointing to allow long-running operations to survive server restarts with zero state loss.

flagshipSystems.title: Enterprise Support & Intelligent Tool Router
flagshipSystems.tagline: Permission-Scoped Tool Execution, Dynamic Intent Routing, & End-to-End Tracing
flagshipSystems.problem: Enterprise customer support teams struggle with high ticket volumes, siloed data systems (CRM, knowledge bases, ticketing APIs), and the risk of hallucinated or unauthorized actions by chatbots.
flagshipSystems.solution: Built a permission-aware assistant utilizing fast intent classification, sandboxed API execution via MCP, and continuous tracing with OpenTelemetry to resolve technical queries autonomously.

pipeline.name: Query Ingestion
pipeline.detail: Handles multi-channel queries with rate limiting, user session tracking, and tenant authorization tokens.
pipeline.tradeoff: Authentication checks at the edge add ~4ms but prevent cross-tenant data leakage.

pipeline.name: Intent Classifier
pipeline.detail: Classifies queries into FAQ (cached), technical lookup (RAG), account action (Tool Call), or human escalation.
pipeline.tradeoff: Small model routing saves 80% cost on trivial queries while reserving large models for complex reasoning.

pipeline.name: LangGraph Execution
pipeline.detail: Executes sandboxed tools with RBAC token verification before any external database mutation.
pipeline.tradeoff: Fine-grained permissions prevent agent privilege escalation in enterprise environments.

pipeline.name: Observability & Guardrails
pipeline.detail: Traces token consumption, execution latency, tool invocation logs, and response safety guardrails.
pipeline.tradeoff: Telemetry payload logging requires structured scrubbing of PII to maintain compliance.

engineeringDecisions: Implemented semantic cache layer to instantly resolve frequent common enterprise queries without LLM invocation.
Restricted tool invocation to schema-validated Pydantic models with automated parameter boundary checks.
Instrumented complete OpenTelemetry traces to monitor end-to-end latency per sub-system.

flagshipSystems.title: Document Intelligence & PDF Chatbot
flagshipSystems.tagline: Interactive GenAI RAG Application with Real-Time Vector QA & In-Browser PDF Parsing
flagshipSystems.problem: Extracting answers and synthesizing cross-document insights from dense multi-page academic papers and technical specifications without tedious manual searching.
flagshipSystems.solution: Built a responsive Streamlit and LangChain application enabling real-time document upload, in-memory chunking, vector indexing, and grounded conversational question answering.

pipeline.name: PDF Upload
pipeline.detail: Parses user-uploaded documents and extracts text chunks in real-time.
pipeline.tradeoff: In-memory processing ensures immediate feedback without storing user documents permanently.

pipeline.name: Vector QA Engine
pipeline.detail: Performs cosine similarity search against indexed document chunks for relevant paragraph selection.
pipeline.tradeoff: Lightweight vector store fits inside serverless deployment limits.

pipeline.name: Streamlit Interface
pipeline.detail: Delivers real-time streaming answers with source snippet references and chat history persistence.
pipeline.tradeoff: Streamlit enables rapid iterative deployment for public demonstration.

engineeringDecisions: Configured custom chunk overlap to preserve conversational context across split paragraphs.
Employed streaming LLM tokens to minimize perceived time-to-first-token (TTFT) for user queries.

howIBuildStages.title: UNDERSTAND
howIBuildStages.subtitle: Problem Definition & Task Framing
howIBuildStages.description: Deconstruct the business challenge. Determine whether the problem actually requires an LLM, a deterministic algorithm, or hybrid retrieval. Frame context boundaries and failure modes.

howIBuildStages.title: RETRIEVE
howIBuildStages.subtitle: Embeddings · Search · Hybrid Retrieval
howIBuildStages.description: Design the retrieval topology. Implement semantic dense indexing with pgvector alongside sparse BM25 token matching, unified via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and Cross-Encoder reranking.

howIBuildStages.title: REASON
howIBuildStages.subtitle: LLMs · Structured Outputs · Tool Calling
howIBuildStages.description: Select the optimal model tier. Enforce structured outputs using Pydantic schemas, strict grounding prompts, and constrained function calling to eliminate hallucinations.

howIBuildStages.title: ORCHESTRATE
howIBuildStages.subtitle: LangGraph · Agents · MCP
howIBuildStages.description: Structure multi-agent coordination. Build stateful cyclical workflows with LangGraph, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool standardizations, state checkpointing, and human-in-the-loop gates.

howIBuildStages.title: EVALUATE
howIBuildStages.subtitle: RAGAS · DeepEval · Retrieval Metrics
howIBuildStages.description: Measure before shipping. Run automated CI/CD evaluation pipelines measuring Faithfulness, Answer Relevance, Context Precision, and Context Recall against synthetic test suites.

howIBuildStages.title: DEPLOY
howIBuildStages.subtitle: FastAPI · Docker · Cloud
howIBuildStages.description: Containerize for production. Build high-throughput async FastAPI backends, package into lean Docker containers, and deploy to scalable cloud environments with rate limiting.

howIBuildStages.title: OBSERVE
howIBuildStages.subtitle: Tracing · Logging · Latency · Cost
howIBuildStages.description: Track telemetry end-to-end. Capture prompt/completion tokens, per-node execution latencies, tool execution logs, and cost analytics via OpenTelemetry and structured logging.

principles.detail: Quickly build working proofs-of-concept to validate feasibility before committing to heavy infrastructure.
Never guess bottlenecks. Profile token usage, network hops, and retrieval latency with empirical instrumentation.
Ground LLMs with high-precision contextual knowledge rather than relying on parametric memory.
Equip agents with deterministic tools (SQL, calculators, verified APIs) for factual correctness.
Rigorously benchmark retrieval and synthesis using RAGAS and automated test suites before claiming production readiness.
Instrument end-to-end tracing and cost attribution so no agent execution is an unmonitored black box.
